words.definition: High-speed temporary storage that keeps frequently used data close to the processor so it can be fetched fast.
words.example: Clearing the browser cache fixed the broken images.

words.definition: Software written to harm, hijack, or spy on a computer — viruses, trojans, and ransomware are all malware.
words.example: That popup was malware pretending to be a virus scan.

words.definition: A security barrier that controls what network traffic is allowed in and out of a device or network.
words.example: The office firewall blocked the suspicious login attempt.

words.definition: A scam that tricks you into handing over passwords or card numbers by pretending to be a trusted source.
words.example: The email looked like it was from the bank, but it was phishing.

words.definition: The amount of data that can move through a connection in a given time — think of it as the width of the pipe.
words.example: Four video calls at once ate all the bandwidth.

words.definition: Scrambling data so only someone with the key can read it — the backbone of private messaging and shopping.
words.example: Encryption keeps your card number safe at checkout.

words.definition: The low-level software baked into a device that tells its hardware how to boot and behave.
words.example: A firmware update made the printer print faster.

words.definition: A Solid-State Hybrid Drive — a hard disk paired with a small flash cache for quicker starts.
words.example: The old laptop felt new again after an SSHD swap.

words.definition: The delay between an action and its response — low latency means snappy, high latency means laggy.
words.example: Gamers chase the lowest possible latency.

words.definition: A second copy of your files kept separate from the originals so a crash isn't a catastrophe.
words.example: Her photos survived the flood because of a real backup.

words.definition: The tiny single-colour dot that, by the millions, makes up everything you see on a screen.
words.example: A dead pixel showed up as a black speck on the display.

words.definition: Relating to heat — in PCs, thermal design is how a machine sheds the heat its chips produce.
words.example: New thermal paste dropped the CPU temp by 12 degrees.

words.definition: An isolated space where untrusted software can run without touching the rest of your system.
words.example: The browser opens downloads in a sandbox.

words.definition: How long a system has been running without a crash or reboot — a measure of reliability.
words.example: The server hit 400 days of uptime.

words.definition: A small program that lets the operating system talk to a piece of hardware like a printer or GPU.
words.example: A missing driver left the webcam dark.

words.definition: Unwanted bulk messages — junk mail, fake offers, and the noise that clogs your inbox.
words.example: The filter caught 30 spam emails overnight.

words.definition: Stealthy malware that hides deep in a system to keep itself and other attacks invisible.
words.example: The scan found a rootkit buried in the boot sector.

words.definition: A go-between server that fetches web content on your behalf, masking where the request came from.
words.example: The office routes traffic through a proxy.

words.definition: The core of an operating system that manages memory, hardware, and running programs.
words.example: A kernel panic froze the Mac mid-edit.

words.definition: A small update that fixes a bug or closes a security hole in software.
words.example: Install the patch before the flaw gets exploited.

words.definition: To run a chip faster than its stock speed for more performance — at the cost of heat and stability.
words.example: He overclocked the GPU for a few extra frames.

words.definition: A network of hijacked devices controlled together, often used to flood websites or send spam.
words.example: The malware turned the PCs into a botnet.

words.definition: A unit of digital info — 8 bits, roughly one character of text.
words.example: That file is about two million bytes.

words.definition: A program that turns human-readable code into machine language the CPU can run.
words.example: The compiler caught the typo before it ever ran.

words.definition: A background process that runs quietly to handle printing, updates, or network tasks.
words.example: The print daemon restarted when the spool jammed.

words.definition: Wired networking that uses a cable for a fast, steady connection.
words.example: She switched to Ethernet and the lag vanished.

words.definition: The device that connects your local network to the wider internet — usually your router.
words.example: The gateway handed out a fresh IP after the reboot.

words.definition: A fixed-length fingerprint of data, so even a tiny change makes a totally different hash.
words.example: The download's hash proved the file wasn't tampered with.

words.definition: The box that turns the signal from your provider into data your network can use.
words.example: A modem reboot fixed the 'no internet' light.

words.definition: Any single device or point in a network that sends, receives, or forwards data.
words.example: Every smart bulb is a node on the home network.

words.definition: A small chunk of data wrapped with an address and sent across a network.
words.example: Lost packets are why a video call freezes for a second.

words.definition: A numbered doorway on a device that a specific kind of network traffic uses.
words.example: The game needed port 25565 opened to host friends.

words.definition: A request for information — usually a question you ask a database or search engine.
words.example: The slow query was missing an index.

words.definition: Random Access Memory — fast, short-term working space the PC clears when you power off.
words.example: Adding more RAM stopped the tab-crashing.

words.definition: The box that directs traffic between your devices and the internet.
words.example: A router reboot is the first fix for most Wi-Fi woes.

words.definition: A software endpoint — one end of a two-way connection between programs.
words.example: The app opened a socket to stream the update.

words.definition: One independent line of execution inside a program, running alongside others.
words.example: Too many threads at once can thrash the CPU.

words.definition: Malware disguised as something harmless, like a fake game or tool.
words.example: The 'free' optimizer was actually a trojan.

words.definition: The universal plug almost every peripheral uses to connect and charge.
words.example: A USB hub turned one port into six.

words.definition: Simulated in software rather than physical — like a machine that isn't really a box.
words.example: The virtual server boots in seconds, no hardware needed.

words.definition: A self-copying malicious program that spreads by attaching to other files.
words.example: The old virus hid in the boot sector.
